subject: Initial meeting recap — data protection & logging scope
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@carebridge.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial meeting recap — data protection & logging scope

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up below to capture what we heard, confirm success criteria, and propose next steps so we all have the same frame. Please flag anything we missed.

Summary of what you told us
- Pain: current LLM experiments are failing legal review because logs include free-text PII (SSNs, PHI snippets) from user inputs and chat transcripts. Ops can’t safely keep those logs in plain text.
- Risk tolerance: CareBridge needs a vendor that can demonstrate strict PII controls (redaction or no-logging), auditable model invocation records, and customer-managed keys.
- Current stack: internal web app (Node/TS) -> API gateway -> third-party LLM endpoints (some managed, some self-hosted). Logs are shipped to a centralized ELK stack; retention defaults to 2 years.
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA-adjacent requirements for certain workflows; legal will require a DPA + SOC 2 evidence before production signoff.

Success criteria you outlined
1) No raw PII persisted in logs or storage accessible to vendor by default (either redacted at ingress or explicitly disabled).
2) Ability to set an adjustable retention window down to 30 days for full request/response payloads and shorter for metadata.
3) Field-level redaction for structured fields and heuristic redaction for free-text (configurable).
4) Audit trail: immutable invocation logs (who, when, model id, model version, route) with exportable CSV for audits.
5) Customer-managed KMS support (bring-your-own-key) and proof of secure key handling.
6) SOC 2 documentation and a timely security questionnaire turnaround for legal.

What we can deliver immediately (next 72 hours)
- Attach SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-2024.pdf) and a short whitepaper on redaction strategies (redaction-options.pdf).
- Share an initial data retention mapping spreadsheet so you can mark required retention for each route (carebridge-initial-map.xlsx).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Marcus (inference infra) to validate feasibility of per-route retention and redaction logic.

Proposed next steps
- Jordan: confirm who from legal should receive the SOC 2 + DPA; legal@carebridge.io is fine if there are others please add. (Action: Jordan — by Tue 5/11)
- Marcus/Redwood: propose two calendar options for a tech session next week (Action: Marcus — by Mon 5/10)
- Both teams: fill the retention mapping spreadsheet with current routes and required retention (Action: CareBridge ops — by Fri 5/14)

If this aligns with your expectations I’ll attach the SOC2 PDF and the mapping sheet now — I’ve included the files and a HubSpot link to the record below.

Thanks — Kim

Subject: Re: Initial meeting recap — data protection & logging scope

Kim / team — thanks for the succinct recap, this matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from legal/ops that will be gating:

Clarifications / constraints
- Retention: default retention for full transcripts must be <= 90 days for most clinical-facing routes; for analytics-only routes we can go up to 1 year but must mask identifiers. Some regulated flows require 30-day retention.
- Redaction: we require both structured field masking (explicit PII attributes) and a probabilistic redaction layer for free text before it leaves our environment — ideally at the API gateway. Acceptable to do either: redaction-in-flight (ingress) or an architecture where raw payloads never persist to vendor logs.
- Encryption: BYOK (KMS) is a requirement for production; HSM-backed key storage preferred for subsystem dealing with PHI.
- Audit: audit logs must record request id, route, model-id+version, timestamp, and a hashed user id (no raw user identifier). Exportable within 72 hours on request.
- Third-party processing: legal will not approve transmission of unencrypted PHI to third-party processors without explicit contractual controls.

Next steps on our side
- I’ll have legal confirm the DPA reviewers by EOD Tue 5/11 (sending to legal@carebridge.io).
- Ops will start filling the retention mapping spreadsheet and should have a first pass by Fri 5/14.
- Proposed tech call: Tue 5/11 at 10:00 PT or Wed 5/12 at 09:00 PT — either works; invite Marcus and the infra/gov engineer who owns the gateway.

We appreciate the attachments — downloading now. Expect legal feedback after they review the SOC2 summary.

Best,
Jordan
